What is this addressing?

Doing checks with `"clang" in $CC`/`"clang++" in $CXX` is meant to support potentially prefixed binary names, e.g. with a target triple. For example our Linux SDKs (currently using GCC) provide `x86_64-godot-linux-gnu-gcc` as one of the options someone could pass to `CC`.

I don't know if there are actual uses for this currently out in the wild, but I'd be wary of breaking some workflows and forcing users to use their `PATH`'s `clang` when they wanted to use a specific toolchain via a manually specified `CC`/`CXX`.
